title: Warning about unusable key file and I cannot find where that path even comes from...
author: meyergru
body_snippet:
Some of my saved connections try to use an old key file and I cannot for the life of me find why/where this setting comes from. I see lines like this at the start of the PuTTY session:

```
Unable to use key file "C:\Users\xxx\.ssh\id_ed25519" (OpenSSH SSH-2 private key (new format))
Using username "www".
Authenticating with public key "pageant@machine" from agent
...

```

You said:

> **3. Phantom key file prompt after install** That prompt comes from pageant (PuTTY's agent), not from mRemoteN...

comments.author: robertpopa22
comments.snippet:
Found it — and my earlier answer on #90 was wrong, apologies. The path is **not** coming from pageant or the registry: **mRemoteNG itself was injecting it.**

When a connection has no private key and no stored password, mRemoteNG auto-discovers a key from `~/.ssh/` and passes `-i <key>` to PuTTY (added in #1602). It was offering bare OpenSSH keys (`id_ed25519`, `id_rsa`, …). PuTTY/plink can only load a *new-format* OpenSSH key via `-i` on newer versions; older ones print exactly your message — `...
